newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields little changed, crown firmer.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields little changed, crown firmer.

text.p: 1515 GMT - Swedish debt yields closed little changed while the crown firmed sharply against the dollar on Monday. Dealers said trading was thin, with most eyes on moves in dollar/mark and foreign debt markets.

Focus tomorrow will be on the dollar and with an improving sentiment in the market, some dealers expect the crown to test the 4.40 level versus the mark later this week. The repo rate is seen unchanged at 4.10 percent at Tuesday's announcement.
* Six-month T-bills remain unchanged at 4.03 percent
* Nine-year bond yields are also flat at 6.69 percent
* The mark eases to 4.4395 crowns from 4.4480 late on Friday
Swedish debt yields closed little changed on Monday while the crown firmed sharply against the dollar.
Dealers said the crown benefited from general pressure on the dollar after this weekend's G7-meeting.
"Trading has been thin but with some of the positive sentiment returning, I think we can see a test of the 4.40 crown level against the mark later this week," said one dealer.
Debt yields fell a few basis points in early trade but at closing time, both six-month T-bills and nine-year bond yields were unchanged at 4.03 percent and 6.69 percent, respectively.
The crown posted strong gains against the dollar but also gained some ground against the mark.
At 1515 GMT, the dollar had plunged to 7.3394 crowns from 7.4379 crowns late on Friday, while the mark eased to 4.4395 crowns from 4.4480 crowns.
But although the crown firmed on Monday, its weakening streak last week is seen preventing the Riksbank from cutting the repo rate at Tuesday's one-week repo operation.
A Reuter survey showed all of twelve analysts expecting the repo rate to be kept at 4.10 percent on Tuesday.
